## AppPorts v1.9.0 更新说明 [English](#english-release-notes) · [直链下载](https://file.shimoko.com/AppPorts) ·  [赞助](https://pic.cdn.shimoko.com/thanks.png)

### 总结

这次，我们想让你更省心地给 Mac 腾空间。**1.9.0 加入了保留应用原始签名的 APFS 容器数据迁移**，让聊天记录、图片视频等适用的应用数据也能搬到外置盘，应用仍按原来的路径读取。希望你能少一点因为空间不足而做取舍，多留一些喜欢的应用和想留住的内容。我们还加入了数据卷自动接回，让日常连接外置盘后的准备工作更轻松。

打开 AppPorts，你也会发现找数据、看空间更顺手了。我们重新整理了目录树，加上搜索筛选、展开动画、可调高度的信息栏和零字节目录开关，**哪些数据占地方、这次能腾出多少空间，看得更明白**。针对部分应用迁移后或恢复到本地后找不到关联数据的问题，我们也补上了识别支持；这项修复无需重新迁移或重新签名，更新后重新扫描即可。

第一次使用有新的分步引导，权限没准备好、应用信息没读全，也会告诉你下一步该怎么做。我们还完善了原始应用备份、失败恢复和 macOS 27 修复指引，希望你从第一次搬家到日常使用，都能少一点摸索，多一点安心。感谢大家把使用中遇到的问题告诉我们，这些反馈都在帮助 AppPorts 变得更好用。

### 升级提示

**准备升级 macOS 27：请先更新并打开一次 AppPorts。** 新版需要这次启动来更新已经安装的后台重签名脚本，加入系统版本保护；只下载新版还不够。升级后打开 AppPorts，会关闭「开机自动重签名」并停止、移除旧任务；若未能完成清理，设置页会提示重试。

**旧方式迁移的应用打不开时，先查看修复步骤。** 连接原来的外置盘，完全退出要修复的应用，然后在应用列表中找到带「签名已替换」标记的应用，点击「修复」。先还原通过旧符号链接迁移的容器数据，再恢复原始签名或从官方渠道重装。保留现有数据和备份，不要再次重签名。详细步骤见 [macOS 27 升级与修复说明](https://docs-appports.shimoko.com/macos-27.html)。

已经通过 APFS 挂载迁移的目录无需仅为签名修复而还原。更新 AppPorts 不会自动转换旧迁移，也不会自动恢复曾被替换的签名。

### 新功能

**APFS 容器数据迁移** — 支持将 `Containers`、`Group Containers` 下的应用数据迁移到外置盘，在原目录挂载专用的数据卷，保留应用原有签名和访问路径。提供挂载、卸载和还原操作。默认模式下，容器数据使用这套方案；其他数据目录继续使用各自适用的迁移方式。

**容器数据卷管理与自动接回** — 数据目录新增「已挂载」「待挂载」「外置盘未连接」等状态，按当前情况提供挂载、卸载和还原操作。迁移成功后安装后台挂载任务，在登录或连接外置盘时尝试接回数据卷；最后一条挂载记录还原后自动移除任务。后台任务独立运行，不需要打开主窗口；旧系统的管理员授权限制见下方使用提示。

**全新首次使用引导与准备检查** — 首次启动按步骤介绍迁移方式，并检查完全磁盘访问权限、App 管理权限和外部存储。缺少权限时可直接前往对应的系统设置；还没选外置盘也可以先进入应用。完成引导后记住进度，后续可在「设置 → 准备情况」重新检查。

**核对当前运行的 AppPorts** — 准备检查中显示当前进程对应的应用版本、构建号和实际路径，并提供「在 Finder 中显示」和「复制路径」。完全磁盘访问检查区分通过、被拒绝和无法确认三种结果，方便排查升级后授权仍指向旧副本的情况。此功能检查当前进程的实际访问能力，不能直接读取并比对系统授权列表中的版本。

**零字节目录显示开关** — 工具目录和应用数据默认隐藏已经确认是零字节的本地目录，可通过「显示零字节目录」开关恢复显示，并记住选择。仍在计算、读取不完整，以及已链接、已挂载或待接回的目录继续保留；有匹配子目录时保留必要的父级层次。

**签名问题识别与修复面板** — 根据 AppPorts 的原始签名记录和真实应用当前的签名判断是否发生替换，在应用行提供修复入口。修复面板按实际情况展示容器数据还原、原始签名恢复或官方重装步骤，并提供重新检查和文档入口。

**完整原始应用备份与恢复** — 重签名前保存完整的原始应用，恢复时还原其签名、授权及文件元数据，无需开发者私钥。只有旧签名记录的用户，可以选择匹配的官方原版应用补救。当前应用与备份不匹配时，会说明原因并保留恢复材料。

### 界面与目录浏览

**更清楚的数据目录树** — 保留左侧应用列表，右侧按目录类型展示父子关系。目录行采用系统文件夹图标，类型由分组图标和标题说明；调整行高、缩进、字号与间距，对齐名称、大小、状态和操作。迁移、还原等常用操作直接显示在对应行。

**展开与折叠合并为一个按钮** — 顶部按钮根据当前状态切换「展开全部」和「折叠全部」。分组、文件夹及全部目录的展开收起加入过渡动画，箭头随状态旋转，并遵循系统「减少动态效果」设置。

**可上下拖动的信息栏** — 拖动目录列表下方的把手调整信息栏高度，为目录列表或路径详情分配更多空间。信息栏可压缩为紧凑的单行路径，同时保留复制和 Finder 定位操作；展开后展示本地路径、外部路径和目录说明，长内容可单独滚动。

**搜索与键盘浏览** — 支持按目录名称、路径和说明搜索，与类型、状态和优先级筛选配合使用。匹配结果保留父级上下文并自动展开。支持方向键选择、展开和折叠目录，以及复制所选目录路径；鼠标选择不再强行将目录滚动到列表中央。

**各页面的视觉风格统一** — 应用迁移保留原有双栏和操作流程，微调本地、外部面板的标题、图标和按钮比例，使其与下方列表对齐。数据目录、目录迁移及顶部工具栏采用更一致的底色、圆角和间距，减少分隔线、厚重阴影和突兀的白色区块；以轻量的颜色区分区域、选中和悬停状态，并兼顾浅色与深色外观。

### 改进

**应用数据识别更完整** — 改进迁移到外置盘的原生应用、iOS 包装应用，以及恢复到本地后的应用数据扫描，按真实应用信息查找关联目录，并保留原有的名称匹配。这项修复不改变迁移、签名或 Dock 的操作流程，也不需要重新迁移、重新签名或额外授权；更新后重新扫描即可。

**应用信息没读全时给出明确提示** — 应用信息无法读取时，保留通过名称找到的数据，在页面内提示结果可能不完整，不再把识别失败简单显示为「未找到关联数据目录」。如果真实应用路径不可用，会提示检查路径；应用位于外置盘时，连接磁盘后刷新即可重新识别。切换应用或重新扫描时清除旧提示，避免混淆。

**可释放空间估算更准确** — 只汇总当前筛选范围内可迁移的本地目录，父子目录及重复路径只计算一次；已链接、已挂载到外置盘的数据及其子目录不再计入本机可释放空间。对于微信等包含受保护父目录的应用，仍正确统计其中允许迁移的子目录。

**读取不完整时明确说明** — 目录枚举或大小测量失败时，保留已读取结果，目录显示「至少…」或「无法读取」，汇总区域显示「空间统计不完整」，避免把部分数据或读取失败当成完整大小、零字节目录。权限被拒绝时提供「检查访问权限」入口，并可查看受影响路径。

**刷新重新测量目录大小** — 刷新时重新读取大小，避免沿用应用写入数据前的旧结果；目录挂载状态变化或子目录内容变化时同步处理相关缓存。扫描状态持续到大小计算结束，期间使用固定尺寸的系统进度指示器，避免刷新图标旋转偏心。

**迁移前先说明条件和下一步** — 点击「迁移」后，先检查外部存储是否连接、格式、加密状态及可用空间。可以直接选择或更换存储，继续检查刚才选中的目录；条件不满足时说明原因，并提供保留现状和查看准备方法的选项。

**重签名先在工作副本完成** — 校验备份、在工作副本上重签名并确认结果后，再替换真实应用。操作期间应用内容发生变化、备份损坏或替换失败时，保留现有应用和恢复材料；恢复原始签名前等待旧后台重签名任务停止，避免刚恢复又被改写。

**应用更新后的备份更准确** — 识别经过验证、开发者身份一致的官方更新或重装版本，建立新的恢复点，并归档旧记录与旧快照，避免用旧版本备份覆盖新版本应用。选择官方原版补救时，同时核对应用标识、版本和开发者签名。

**登录与插盘后的挂载更及时** — 调整后台任务的启动方式，减少重复磁盘查询；外置盘识别较慢时持续等待连接事件并有限重试，等待期间让出操作资源。每次挂载后检查卷是否真正落在原目录，遇到系统提前挂到其他位置的情况，会重新定位并接回。

**后台任务路径更可靠** — 更新或移动 AppPorts 后，启动时同步后台任务的程序路径。从 DMG 或系统临时隔离路径运行时，先提示将 AppPorts 放入「应用程序」，避免安装指向临时位置的任务。旧系统需要管理员权限时，可通过系统密码框重试挂载。

**减少辅助数据卷的干扰** — 数据卷默认不显示在 Finder 边栏和桌面，并添加 Spotlight 索引排除标记，减少额外占用。还原数据时跳过卷自身的索引、事件记录等辅助文件；后台任务无事可做时减少日志输出。

**外置盘未连接时保护原目录** — 未挂载的目录保持不可写，减少应用在本机另建一份数据的风险。重新挂载前检查目录是否为空；发现本地文件或其他卷占用时停止操作，避免遮住已有数据。使用应用前仍需先连接外置盘并确认挂载完成。

**迁移失败后保留明确的恢复入口** — 迁移前检查外置盘空间，切换路径前保留本地安全副本。操作失败时尝试恢复原目录；无法完成恢复时，保留可用副本并说明所在路径和数据卷信息。

**还原与清理分别处理** — 还原前检查本机空间，先停用对应目录的自动挂载，再切换回本地数据。数据已恢复但后续清理失败时，单独保存待清理记录并提供重试，重试不会再次复制或覆盖已经恢复的数据。还可明确选择仅移除清理记录、保留现有副本。

**更严格的操作对象与记录校验** — 挂载、卸载和还原前核对数据卷身份，只处理 AppPorts 管理的目标。迁移记录无法读取时保留原文件；卸载后只删除空挂载点。后台挂载、手动迁移和签名操作协调执行，避免同时修改同一份数据。

**长操作之后重新检查应用状态** — 等待后台任务、获取操作权限或完成签名备份后，再次确认应用是否运行、入口是否仍指向同一应用。批量还原过程中应用重新启动时，停止后续目录的操作。经典模式的沙盒重签名仍需针对当前真实应用单独确认。

**确认弹窗更清楚** — 统一迁移、还原和签名相关提示，长说明可滚动，标题与操作按钮保持可见。取消和 Esc 行为一致，需要确认风险的操作在勾选后才可继续；执行下一步前先关闭当前弹窗，避免按钮无响应或后续弹窗被覆盖。

**经典模式保留为可选项** — 「经典数据迁移模式」默认关闭，开启前需要确认风险，设置卡片新增「查看完整说明」。macOS 27 上仍可手动开启经典模式，但开机自动重签名保持停用；推荐使用保留原始签名的挂载迁移。

**更多异常场景的回归覆盖** — 新增挂载与还原、外置盘延迟上线、目录占用、备份损坏、应用更新、后台重签名停用和清理重试等测试；补充可释放空间去重、读取失败、零字节筛选、当前应用权限检查，以及赞助名单线上优先与离线回退测试。本次应用数据识别修复另新增 48 个回归测试，覆盖迁移与恢复后的应用、外置目标缺失后恢复、短名称误匹配及异常链接等情况；本地全量 474 个测试通过，相关测试已加入持续集成。

### 文档与项目支持

- 新增 APFS 挂载迁移、容器数据与签名身份、外置盘格式选择和 macOS 27 修复说明，补充常见故障、权限和还原指引。
- macOS 27 文档将修复步骤前移，优先提供应用内的操作路径，并说明升级系统前应先更新、打开一次 AppPorts。
- 同步简体中文、繁体中文、英语、日语、韩语、德语、法语和西班牙语文档及导航，新增挂载、沙盒和断盘实验记录供进一步查阅；新增界面文案覆盖应用支持的语言，文档入口跟随应用语言。
- 「关于 AppPorts」增加赞助者列表、开源许可证和隐私政策入口，菜单栏新增赞助入口；文档站提供对应的多语言页面。
- 赞助名单以线上 JSON 为权威来源：读取成功后直接采用并更新缓存，不按本地更新时间拦截线上内容；只有网络或解析失败时才依次使用缓存、内置名单。合法的线上空名单同样生效，避免旧名单重新出现。
- 未提供个人链接的赞助者以纯文字显示姓名；赞助金额仅在网站展示，保留最多两位小数，正确显示 `¥0.63` 等金额。本地名单及 README 致谢补充符华；本地 JSON 修改需部署到文档站后，现有安装才会通过线上读取获得新名单。
- 补充项目内的 UI / VI 设计原则，明确颜色、间距、对齐、信息层级和动效的使用方式，便于后续界面调整保持一致。

### 修复

- 修复部分应用迁移到外置盘后，数据扫描误读本地启动入口的信息，导致关联容器遗漏或匹配到无关目录的问题（[#63](https://github.com/wzh4869/AppPorts/issues/63)）。
- 修复 iOS 包装应用及其恢复到本地后，因未读取内层应用信息而找不到关联数据的问题；保留短名称匹配限制，避免扩大误匹配范围。
- 修复应用身份识别失败时仍显示普通空结果、空间汇总未标记不完整的问题；外置目标恢复后，刷新会重新读取应用信息。
- 修复点击目录后列表强行居中，导致原有浏览位置跳动的问题。
- 修复目录大小计算及缓存更新不一致，导致父目录显示小于子目录的问题。
- 修复微信等应用的可释放空间可能混入不可迁移父目录、重复目录或外置数据的问题。
- 修复目录读取失败被当作空目录，或只显示部分空间却没有提示的问题；不存在的可选目录不再被计为读取故障。
- 修复权限检查无法区分「被拒绝」与「暂时无法确认」的问题，避免因检查文件不可用而直接判定未授权。
- 修复部分修复、删除按钮过于突出或未与同行控件对齐的问题。
- 修复最大日志大小选择 `100 MB` 时只显示为 `1` 的问题。
- 修复应用名或 Bundle ID 中的 `CN`、`mac`、`desktop` 等通用词导致容器误匹配的问题，避免把 WPS 等其他应用的数据列入 Trae CN 的修复步骤。
- 修复签名检测可能检查本地启动入口而非外置真实应用的问题；检查失败或外置应用不可读时，显示独立的待检查状态并保留恢复材料。
- 修复有完整原始应用备份时，修复引导仍要求先将外置应用迁回本机的问题；准备覆盖安装时才按需提示这一步。
- 修复从本地已链接应用发起迁回时，误把启动入口当成外置应用本体，提示「本地已存在同名真实文件，无法覆盖」的问题。
- 修复部分确认弹窗操作后未关闭，造成按钮看似无响应或后续提示被覆盖的问题。
- 修复容器路径以 `/private/var` 形式出现时，子目录可能未被扫描的问题。
- 修复没有个人链接的赞助者不显示姓名、赞助网站将小数金额取整的问题。

### 迁移使用提示

- 容器挂载迁移目前需要**未加密的 APFS 外置盘**和 AppPorts 的完全磁盘访问权限。请先将 AppPorts 放入「应用程序」文件夹再使用。其他格式的存储可以继续用于适用的应用或普通目录迁移，容器数据也可以留在本机。详见 [挂载迁移说明](https://docs-appports.shimoko.com/datamigrae/mount-migration.html)。
- 第一次打开迁移后的应用时，如 macOS 询问是否允许访问可移动宗卷，请按提示允许。之后使用应用前先连接外置盘，拔盘前先退出应用并正常推出；重要数据请另行备份。
- macOS 12 等需要管理员授权才能挂载的系统，可能需要打开 AppPorts 并输入系统密码，不能依赖无界面的登录任务自动完成挂载。

### ⚠️ “AppPorts”已损坏，无法打开

如果从 AppPorts 官方发布渠道下载后遇到此提示，可能与 macOS 对未进行 Developer ID 签名和公证的应用进行隔离有关。

确认下载来源后，将 AppPorts 拖入「应用程序」文件夹，再在终端运行：

```shell
xattr -rd com.apple.quarantine /Applications/AppPorts.app
```
releaseNotes.en:
## English Release Notes

### Summary

We want freeing up space on your Mac to feel less like a chore. **Version 1.9.0 adds APFS container data migration that preserves your apps’ original signatures**, so supported app data, including chat history, photos, and videos, can move to an external drive while apps keep reading from their familiar paths. That means fewer difficult choices about which apps or memories to keep. We have also added automatic data-volume reconnection to make getting ready after connecting your drive easier.

Finding your data and understanding your storage should feel easier, too. We have refreshed the directory tree with search and filters, expansion animations, a resizable information panel, and a zero-byte directory toggle. **It is clearer what takes up space and how much a migration can free.** We have also fixed missing data results for some migrated or restored apps. This discovery fix needs no repeat migration or re-signing: update AppPorts and scan again.

New step-by-step guidance helps you get started, with clearer next steps when permissions are missing or app information cannot be fully read. Better original-app backups, failure recovery, and macOS 27 repair guidance are there to make the experience more reassuring, from your first move to everyday use. Thank you for telling us where things get frustrating—your feedback helps make AppPorts easier to use.

### Upgrade Notes

**Before upgrading to macOS 27, update and open AppPorts once.** Launching the new version updates any installed background re-signing script with a system-version check; downloading the update alone is not enough. Opening AppPorts after the macOS upgrade turns off “Auto Re-sign at Login” and stops and removes the old task. If cleanup cannot finish, Settings provides a retry option.

**If an app migrated with the old method no longer opens, start with the repair guide.** Connect the original external drive, fully quit the affected app, and click “Repair” beside an app marked “Signature replaced.” Restore container data migrated through old symbolic links first, then restore the original signature or reinstall from an official source. Keep existing data and backups, and do not re-sign the app again. See [Upgrading to macOS 27 and repairing affected apps](https://docs-appports.shimoko.com/en/macos-27.html).

Directories already using APFS mount migration do not need to be restored solely for signature repair. Updating AppPorts does not automatically convert older migrations or restore previously replaced signatures.

### New Features

**APFS container data migration** — Move app data under `Containers` and `Group Containers` to dedicated volumes on an external drive, mounted at the original directories without changing the app’s signature or data paths. Mount, unmount, and restore operations are available. This is the default method for container data; other directories continue to use their applicable migration methods.

**Container volume management and automatic reconnection** — New directory statuses include “Mounted,” “Pending Mount,” and “External drive not connected,” with the applicable mount, unmount, and restore actions. Successful migration installs a background task that attempts to reconnect volumes at login and when storage connects. It is removed after the final mount record is restored. The task runs without opening the main window; see the administrator-authorization limits for older systems below.

**New first-run guidance and readiness checks** — A step-by-step introduction checks Full Disk Access, App Management permission, and external storage. Missing permissions link to the corresponding System Settings page, and choosing a drive can wait until later. Completing the introduction is remembered. Readiness checks remain available in Settings.

**Identify the running copy of AppPorts** — Readiness checks show the current process’s app version, build, and actual path, with Show in Finder and Copy Path actions. Full Disk Access checks distinguish success, denial, and an unknown result, helping investigate permissions that may still refer to an older app copy. This checks the running process’s actual access; it cannot directly read and compare versions in the system’s authorization list.

**Zero-byte directory toggle** — Tool directories and app data hide confirmed empty local directories by default. “Show zero-byte directories” restores them and remembers the preference. Directories still being measured, incomplete reads, and linked, mounted, or pending-reconnection data remain visible. Parent context is retained when a child matches.

**Signature detection and repair panel** — AppPorts compares its original signing records with the real app’s current signature to identify replacements and provide an inline repair action. The panel shows the applicable steps for restoring container data, recovering the original signature, or reinstalling an official copy, with links to documentation and a way to check again.

**Complete original-app backups and restoration** — Before re-signing, AppPorts saves the complete original app so its signature, entitlements, and file metadata can be restored without the developer’s private key. Users with older signing records can supply a matching official app. If the current app does not match the backup, AppPorts explains the problem and preserves recovery materials.

### Interface and Directory Browsing

**A clearer directory tree** — The app list remains on the left, with data grouped by directory type on the right. Rows use system folder icons, while group icons and titles identify directory types. Refined row heights, indentation, typography, and spacing align names, sizes, statuses, and actions. Common migration and restoration actions appear directly on each row.

**One control for expanding and collapsing** — The toolbar switches between Expand All and Collapse All based on the current state. Groups, folders, and the full tree expand and collapse with transitions and rotating disclosure arrows, respecting the system’s Reduce Motion setting.

**Vertically resizable information panel** — Drag the handle below the directory list to give more space to either the list or its details. The panel can shrink to a compact path row while retaining Copy Path and Show in Finder. Expanding it reveals local and external paths and directory descriptions, with independent scrolling for longer content.

**Search and keyboard navigation** — Search directory names, paths, and descriptions alongside type, status, and priority filters. Results retain parent context and expand automatically. Arrow keys select, expand, and collapse directories, and the selected path can be copied. Mouse selection no longer forces a directory to the center of the list.

**Consistent styling across pages** — App migration retains its two-pane layout and workflow, with refined header, icon, and button proportions aligned to the lists below. Data directories, custom directory migration, and the top toolbar use more consistent backgrounds, corners, and spacing, with fewer dividers, heavy shadows, and abrupt white blocks. Subtle color distinguishes areas, selection, and hover states in light and dark appearances.

### Improvements

**More complete app data discovery** — Improved scanning for native apps moved to external storage, wrapped iOS apps, and apps restored to the Mac. AppPorts reads the real app’s identity to find associated directories while retaining existing name matching. This fix keeps migration, signing, and Dock workflows unchanged and requires no repeat migration, re-signing, or additional permission grants. Update and scan again to use it.

**Clear feedback when app information cannot be read** — Data found by name remains visible, with an inline warning that results may be incomplete. An identity lookup failure is no longer shown as an ordinary “No associated data directories found” result. If the real app path is unavailable, AppPorts suggests checking it; for apps on external storage, reconnect the drive and refresh to retry. Switching apps or starting a new scan clears the previous warning.

**More accurate reclaimable-space estimates** — Totals include only migratable local directories within the current filter, counting parent/child directories and duplicate paths once. Data already linked or mounted externally, including its descendants, is excluded from reclaimable local space. For apps such as WeChat, migratable children inside protected parent directories are still counted correctly.

**Explicit incomplete-read reporting** — If directory discovery or size measurement fails, available results are retained. Directory sizes show “At least…” or “Unable to read,” and the summary reports incomplete space statistics instead of presenting a partial result as complete or treating failed reads as empty directories. Permission denials provide an access-check entry point, and affected paths can be inspected.

**Fresh measurements when refreshing** — Refreshing measures directories again instead of reusing sizes from before an app wrote new data. Related caches account for mount-state changes and child-directory changes. Scanning remains active until size calculation finishes, using a fixed-size system progress indicator to avoid off-center rotation of the refresh icon.

**Clearer checks before migration** — Clicking “Migrate” checks the external storage connection, format, encryption status, and available space. You can choose or change storage and continue checking the selected directory. If the requirements are not met, AppPorts explains why and offers options to keep the current setup or read the preparation guide.

**Re-signing happens on a working copy first** — AppPorts validates the backup, signs a working copy, and verifies the result before replacing the real app. If the app changes during the operation, the backup is damaged, or replacement fails, the current app and recovery materials are retained. Signature restoration waits for old background re-signing tasks to stop so they cannot immediately overwrite the restored app.

**Backups follow verified app updates** — A verified official update or reinstall with the same developer identity creates a new recovery point while archiving the previous record and snapshot. This prevents an older backup from being used to overwrite a newer app. Official originals supplied for recovery are checked for matching app identity, version, and developer signature.

**More timely mounting at login and drive connection** — Adjusted how the background task starts and reduced repeated disk queries. Slow drives are given time to appear through connection events and bounded retries, without holding operation resources while waiting. Each mount is checked to ensure the volume reaches the original directory; volumes mounted elsewhere by macOS are relocated when possible.

**More reliable background-task paths** — Launching AppPorts after moving or updating it refreshes the background task’s executable path. Running from a DMG or a temporary App Translocation path prompts installation in Applications before setting up new mount migrations. Older systems can retry mounting through the system administrator password dialog.

**Less clutter from auxiliary data volumes** — Data volumes are hidden from Finder’s sidebar and desktop by default and marked to exclude them from Spotlight indexing. Restoration skips the volume’s index, event records, and other auxiliary files. Background runs with nothing to do produce less log output.

**Protecting the original directory while storage is offline** — Unmounted directories remain non-writable to reduce the risk of an app creating a second local data set. AppPorts checks that the mount point is empty before reconnecting a volume and stops if local files or another volume occupy it. Connect the drive and confirm mounting is complete before using the app.

**Clearer recovery after migration failures** — AppPorts checks external free space and retains a local safety copy before switching paths. Failed operations attempt to restore the original directory. If recovery cannot complete, available copies are retained and their paths and volume details are reported.

**Restoration and cleanup are handled separately** — AppPorts checks local free space and disables automatic remounting for the directory before switching back to local data. If the data is restored but cleanup fails, a separate pending-cleanup record supports retrying without copying or overwriting restored data again. An explicit option can remove only the cleanup record while preserving existing copies.

**Stronger checks on operation targets and records** — Mount, unmount, and restore operations verify volume identity and act only on managed targets. Unreadable migration records are preserved, and only empty mount points are deleted after unmounting. Background mounting, manual migration, and signing operations are coordinated to avoid changing the same data concurrently.

**App state is checked again after lengthy work** — After waiting for background work, acquiring operation access, or completing a signature backup, AppPorts checks whether the app is running and whether its launch entry still points to the same target. Relaunching an app during batch restoration stops subsequent directory operations. Classic-mode sandbox re-signing still requires separate approval for the current real app.

**Clearer confirmation dialogs** — Migration, restoration, and signing prompts use a consistent layout. Long explanations scroll while titles and action buttons remain visible. Cancel and Esc behave consistently, and operations requiring risk acknowledgment stay unavailable until it is checked. The current dialog closes before the next action to avoid unresponsive buttons or hidden follow-up prompts.

**Classic mode remains optional** — “Classic Data Migration Mode” is off by default and requires risk confirmation. Its Settings card now includes a link to the full documentation. Classic mode can still be enabled manually on macOS 27, but automatic re-signing at login remains disabled. Mount migration that preserves the original signature is recommended.

**Broader regression coverage** — Added tests for mounting and restoration, delayed drives, occupied directories, damaged backups, app updates, disabling background re-signing, and cleanup retries. Further coverage checks reclaimable-space deduplication, failed reads, zero-byte filtering, permissions for the running app, and online-first sponsor loading with offline fallbacks. The app data discovery fix adds another 48 regression tests covering migrated and restored apps, recovery after an external target becomes available, short-name mismatches, and invalid links. All 474 tests passed locally, and the relevant tests have been added to continuous integration.

### Documentation and Project Support

- Added guides for APFS mount migration, container data and signing identity, choosing storage formats, and macOS 27 recovery, with expanded troubleshooting, permission, and restoration instructions.
- The macOS 27 guide puts repair first, starts with actions available in the app, and explains why AppPorts should be updated and opened once before upgrading macOS.
- Updated documentation and navigation in Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, German, French, and Spanish. Added mounting, sandbox, and drive-disconnection experiment records for further reading. New interface text is translated across supported app languages, and documentation links follow the app language.
- “About AppPorts” adds sponsors, open-source licenses, and privacy policy links. The menu bar adds a sponsorship entry, and the documentation site provides the corresponding multilingual pages.
- The published sponsor JSON is authoritative: successful requests replace the list and cache regardless of local timestamps. Only network or decoding failures fall back to the cache, then the bundled list. A valid empty online list is also accepted so outdated entries do not reappear.
- Sponsors without profile links appear as plain-text names. Amounts remain website-only and retain up to two decimal places, correctly showing amounts such as `¥0.63`. 符华 has been added to the local list and README acknowledgments. Local JSON changes must be deployed to the documentation site before existing installations can receive them online.
- Added project UI / VI design guidelines for color, spacing, alignment, information hierarchy, and motion to keep future interface changes consistent.

### Fixes

- Fixed data scans for some externally migrated apps reading the local launch entry’s identity, which could miss associated containers or match unrelated directories ([#63](https://github.com/wzh4869/AppPorts/issues/63)).
- Fixed missing associated data for wrapped iOS apps, including after restoration to the Mac, by reading the inner app’s information. Existing short-name matching restrictions remain in place to avoid broader false matches.
- Fixed failed app identity lookups appearing as normal empty results without marking space estimates as incomplete. Refreshing reads the app information again when the external target becomes available.
- Fixed selecting a directory forcing it to the center of the list and interrupting browsing.
- Fixed inconsistent directory size calculations and cache updates that could show a parent directory as smaller than its children.
- Fixed reclaimable-space estimates for apps such as WeChat potentially including non-migratable parents, duplicate directories, or external data.
- Fixed failed directory reads being treated as empty directories or partial sizes appearing without a warning. Missing optional directories are no longer classified as read failures.
- Fixed permission checks failing to distinguish denial from an unknown result, avoiding a false denial when a probe file is unavailable.
- Fixed some repair and delete controls appearing overly prominent or misaligned with other controls on the row.
- Fixed the maximum log size displaying only `1` when `100 MB` was selected.
- Fixed generic terms such as `CN`, `mac`, and `desktop` in app names or Bundle IDs matching unrelated containers, including WPS data appearing in Trae CN’s repair steps.
- Fixed signature checks potentially inspecting the local launch entry instead of the real external app. Failed checks or inaccessible external apps now have a separate check-pending state, with recovery materials preserved.
- Fixed repair guidance requiring an external app to be moved back locally even when a complete original app backup was available. That step is now shown when needed for an official reinstall.
- Fixed restoration initiated from a local linked app mistaking its launch entry for the real external app and reporting that an existing local file could not be overwritten.
- Fixed some confirmation dialogs remaining open after an action, making buttons appear unresponsive or obscuring follow-up prompts.
- Fixed subdirectories potentially being missed when container paths use the `/private/var` form.
- Fixed missing sponsor names when no profile link was provided and fractional sponsorship amounts being rounded to whole numbers on the website.

### Migration Notes

- Container mount migration currently requires an **unencrypted APFS external drive** and Full Disk Access for AppPorts. Move AppPorts to Applications before using it. Other storage formats can still be used for supported app or ordinary-directory migrations, while container data can stay on the Mac. See [Mount Migration](https://docs-appports.shimoko.com/en/datamigrae/mount-migration.html).
- On the first launch after migration, allow Removable Volumes access if macOS asks. Connect the external drive before using the app, and quit the app and eject the drive normally before disconnecting it. Keep a separate backup of important data.
- On systems requiring administrator authorization for mounting, such as macOS 12, you may need to open AppPorts and enter the system password. The background login task cannot complete that authorization itself.

### ⚠️ “AppPorts” is damaged and can’t be opened

If this appears after downloading AppPorts from an official release channel, it may be related to macOS quarantine checks for apps without Developer ID signing and notarization.

After confirming the download source, move AppPorts to the Applications folder and run:

```shell
xattr -rd com.apple.quarantine /Applications/AppPorts.app
```

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/wzh4869/AppPorts/compare/1.8.1...v1.9.0
